messages.author: 5a584824866a472b
messages.subject: Flip PCA axes
parts:
Hi everyone,

I was wondering if there is an easy way to reverse x or y axes when plotting a PCA done with gm.prcomp. I tried to use the 'flip' command, but that's not working. Warnings say 'flip' is not a graphical parameter...

I would like to flip the x axis here, PC1.

PCA_sym <- gm.prcomp(Sym_Shape)
plot(PCA_sym, axis1 = 1,   axis2 = 2,   flip = 1,  phylo = FALSE)

Thanks!

Aurélien

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Flip PCA axes
parts:
Aurélien,

Make sure that PCA_sym has the right class.  It should be “ordinate” “gm,.prcomp”, if you do class(PCA_sym).  The error you are getting suggests R does not know that PCA_sym is a class gm.prcomp object, and is using the default plot function rather than plot.gm.pcomp.

I tired a few examples and had no problem.

You can always try to use plot.gm.prcomp instead of plot in your syntax, to attempt to force the plot parameters.  Finally, is it possible you are looking at a modern help file for plot.gm.prcomp but using an old version of geomorph?  Your version might predate when the flip argument was added.

Hope this helps!
Mike

messages.author: 088e8a47a714e2a7
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Flip PCA axes
parts:
Hi Aurélien

If I am understanding your question, you are just trying to flip an axis so that the negative and positive ends are swapped, right? If so, I think you can just multiply that axis by -1 to plot it. I usually plot in ggplot2, and I would do it like this:

ggplot(PC_erec, aes(x= - Comp1, y=Comp2))+
...

This would flip PC 1 (Comp 1).

Hope this helps.

Karen

messages.author: 2fc03d53bc863e8d
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Flip PCA axes
parts: It is important to remind everyone plotting in ggplot2 that they need to include the argument coord_fixed() (to ensure an aspect ratio of 1). That is not the default (as it is for plot(gm.prcomp()). I have recently seen many plots of principal components of shape made in ggplot2 that omit that argument, so apparently it is not obvious that this is necessary.
